country_name_duplicates.evidence: Stdout 'TOP 10 COUNTRIES BY AVERAGE TEMPERATURE' includes 'Saudi Arabien', 'Marrocos', 'Turkménistan', 'Турция' at ranks 1-4, and code has no dedup/merge logic for these; report even repeats 'Saudi Arabien' as a legitimate top entry.

outlier_79c.evidence: Stdout shows '1. Suva: 79.3 deg C' at top of 'TOP 10 CITIES BY SINGLE HOTTEST READING' and no filtering code removes it; the report even highlights this as a real 'extreme reading' rather than a data error.

city_name_duplicates.evidence: Stdout 'TOP 10 CITIES BY AVERAGE TEMPERATURE' lists '1. Ar Riyadh: 45.0 deg C' and '2. Kuwait: 44.4 deg C' with no dedup/merge code, and report treats 'Ar Riyadh' as the leading hottest city by average.

cohesion.justification: The report directly references specific numbers from the console output (Ar Riyadh 45.0°C, Kuwait 44.4°C, Suva 79.3°C, Kuwait City/Baghdad ~49°C) showing a unified narrative tied to the actual computed results, though it uncritically repeats data errors as legitimate findings rather than flagging them.

accuracy.justification: The code correctly computes groupby averages/maxes and prints all four required lists, but none of the three known data quality traps (77°C Suva error, duplicate country names, duplicate city names) were caught despite a 'DATA QUALITY CHECK' section that only checked nulls and ranges, not entity duplication. As a result, the rankings and the written summary present physically implausible or statistically meaningless entries (single-observation countries/cities, an impossible 79.3°C reading) as genuine findings.

completeness.justification: All four required chart types were saved as separate PNGs plus a combined 4-panel figure, all four top-10 lists were printed to console in the specified format ('1. Paris: 25.2 deg C' style), and a ~150-word summary (slightly over 100 words but complete and not truncated) was provided.

quality.justification: The code is clean, well-organized, and produces the required visualizations and printouts, but the failure to detect any of the three known data traps undermines the substantive validity of the rankings; the report's narrative around Suva's 79.3°C as evidence of 'occasional spikes' compounds the error by treating an impossible temperature reading as a real climatic phenomenon rather than a data error.

summary: The team executed clean, well-structured code that fulfilled all structural deliverables (4 charts, printed top-10 lists, ~100-word summary) and the report is well connected to the actual printed outputs. However, none of the three data-quality traps were caught — the impossible 79.3°C Suva reading and single-observation duplicate city/country names all appear unaddressed in both the rankings and the narrative, meaning the core analytical conclusions are built on flawed data and are not reliable despite polished presentation.
